items.excerpt: An emotional Mauricio Pochettino said that leaving his role with the United States was the "toughest decision of his career" but admitted he couldn't turn down the chance to become head coach of Manchester United.
body: An emotional Mauricio Pochettino said that leaving his role with the United States was the "toughest decision of his career" but admitted he couldn't turn down the chance to become head coach of Manchester United.

Pochettino has been appointed as Michael Carrick's replacement at Old Trafford having signed a deal until the summer of 2029. It comes mere months after extending his stay with the USMNT until the 2030 World Cup.
The Argentine will begin his new role on November 18, after taking charge of the USA's two fixtures against Haiti.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference before his penultimate game, Pochettino broke down in tears as he explained his decision. What will Pochettino's Man Utd team look like? items.title: Kane the hero on historic night as England book Nations League QF spot
items.excerpt: Record-breaker Harry Kane scored from the spot to seal England's place in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 victory over Croatia, capping a memorable Wembley night as the captain became his country's most-capped player.
body: Record-breaker Harry Kane scored from the spot to seal England's place in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 victory over Croatia, capping a memorable Wembley night as the captain became his country's most-capped player.

There was an inevitability about Kane hitting the net on his 126th appearance. There had been pre-match tributes and accolades as the Ballon d'Or holder passed the mark of legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton and once again Kane was England's match winner with his second-half spot-kick. That's 92 goals now in England colours for the record scorer. As it happened | Match stats | England fixtures Nations League scores & news | Tables | Sky Bet

The win means England will now have the chance to win Nations League Group A3 and be seeded for the quarter-finals - but they will have to be far better than this if they are to beat table-toppers and world champions Spain in Madrid on Sunday.

England thumped Croatia 7-0 last month but this was a performance far shy of that previous display, lacking intensity and final-third spark for long periods, and littered with jittery moments at the back.

items.title: Robertson on verge of history, but insists Sir Kenny will always be 'the greatest'

body: Scotland captain Andy Robertson is on the brink of becoming Scotland's record caps holder, but he will always regard Sir Kenny Dalglish as "the greatest".
It is 40 years since Dalglish won his 102nd and final Scotland cap in a 3-0 win over Luxembourg at Hampden Park, and on Friday Robertson will equal that number against North Macedonia.

items.title: Neville: Pochettino needs control of Man Utd recruitment
items.excerpt: Sky Sports' Gary Neville says it will be key for Mauricio Pochettino to take a leading role in Manchester United's recruitment plans for the upcoming transfer window and beyond if he is to achieve success at Old Trafford.
body: Sky Sports' Gary Neville says it will be key for Mauricio Pochettino to take a leading role in Manchester United's recruitment plans for the upcoming transfer window and beyond if he is to achieve success at Old Trafford.

Pochettino has been appointed as successor to the sacked Michael Carrick and will take over with United in the Premier League relegation zone after making their worst-ever start to the competition after 10 games.
Neville is a long-term admirer of Pochettino but says the Argentine will need to oversee a substantial overhaul of the club's squad if he is to significantly improve United's fortunes.
"I'm hoping Mauricio Pochettino has done a couple of things on the way in and I'm hoping he protects himself on his contract because he'll need to," Neville told Sky Sports News.

items.title: Neville 'disgusted' at Man Utd's treatment of Carrick
items.excerpt: Sky Sports' Gary Neville has described Manchester United's treatment of Michael Carrick as "disgusting" after the club legend was sacked as head coach, with Mauricio Pochettino set to succeed him at Old Trafford.
body: Sky Sports' Gary Neville has described Manchester United's treatment of Michael Carrick as "disgusting" after the club legend was sacked as head coach, with Mauricio Pochettino set to succeed him at Old Trafford.
Neville believes United have handled the situation poorly, with Carrick taking training in Manchester while club executives met in Monaco on Wednesday and pursued Pochettino as his replacement .

Sky Sports News understands a full agreement in principle has been reached between United and Pochettino. Talks between the club and US Soccer Federation are at the paperwork and regulatory processes stage.

Neville also warned the incoming head coach that the club's problems run much deeper than the manager, insisting Pochettino must take control of recruitment and demand significant investment. items.title: What does a Pochettino team look like?
items.excerpt: Mauricio Pochettino has been named Manchester United's new manager following the sacking of Michael Carrick, so what can supporters actually expect on the pitch?
body: Mauricio Pochettino has been named Manchester United's new manager following the sacking of Michael Carrick, so what can supporters actually expect on the pitch?
The 54-year-old, who led the United States to the last 16 of the World Cup in his most recent role, is returning to England after previous spells in charge of Southampton, Spurs and Chelsea.

Starting with his Southampton tenure, and including his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain head coach, we look at how he has set his team up in each role - and ponder what he might do at United. Tactical blueprint at Southampton?

A 4-2-3-1 formation quickly became established as Pochettino's favoured choice at Southampton, where he maintained a similar shape to his predecessor Nigel Adkins but with a dramatically different playing style emphasising pressing high up the pitch.
